summary: Inference platform that continuously tunes models, engines, kernels, and hardware.
editor_note: Inference optimization becomes a continuous loop: agents learn traffic and constraints, search across models, engines, kernels, and accelerators, then deploy the best performance-per-dollar configuration. A live app and published AMD work make this more concrete than a one-off benchmark service. The cross-hardware bet grows stronger as silicon fragments; the risk is that clouds or chip vendors bundle similar automation.

sources.label: Wing review of Wafer's multi-silicon platform

product_evidence.claim: Wafer continuously searches across the model, inference engine, kernels, and hardware for a deployment matched to a workload's traffic and constraints.
The product exposes a live application and publishes workload-specific optimization evidence across AMD and other inference infrastructure.

market_context.primary_user: AI infrastructure teams operating latency- and cost-sensitive production inference workloads.
market_context.differentiation: Autonomous performance engineers continually retune the full serving stack across heterogeneous accelerators instead of optimizing one deployment once.
market_context.why_now: Inference demand is rising while AMD, TPUs, Trainium, Cerebras, and custom chips make hardware selection more workload-specific.

risks.claim: Clouds, chip vendors, or serving platforms may bundle similar optimization and reduce room for an independent layer.
risks.basis: Wafer's advantage depends on cross-hardware neutrality and accumulated optimization traces remaining more valuable than vendor-native tooling.
